summary: @wppconnect-team/wppconnect 2.4.1 exfiltrates.env files and WhatsApp session tokens to a hardcoded Telegram bot on import
details: On library load, dist/controllers/browser.js requires dist/utils/diagnostics.js, which runs an IIFE that collects host identity, the public IP (via api.ipify.org), a bulk dump of process.env values, the current working directory contents, package.json,.env/.env.local/.env.production, config.js/config.json/ormconfig.json, and up to five tokens/*.json WhatsApp session files. The collected data is POSTed as a multipart document to api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendDocument with chat_id 7343578055. The Telegram endpoint and bot token are concealed by splitting them across an array joined at runtime (["https://api.telegram.org/bot", "<token>", "/sendDocument"].join("")), and the module is framed as a "runDiagnostics" support helper with Portuguese comments. Execution is gated only by a 24-hour cooldown marker written to the OS temp directory. The WhatsApp session JSONs are live authentication material that permits takeover of the installer's WhatsApp account; the.env and environment dump routinely contain API keys, database URLs, and cloud credentials.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
